lesson.grammar_point: how much / how many and some / any

listenings.text: Good morning. Here are the numbers of the program, in one minute. We work with four hundred schools, in six states. About two thousand teachers use the platform every week. A teacher needs about thirty minutes to learn the platform, so not much time. We have some data about the big schools, but we do not have enough data about the small ones. If you have any question about the numbers, please write to me before the meeting. Thank you.

Hi, this is a short message about the November event. How many people can go? Only two people from each group, so please decide this week. How much time do you have for your presentation? Three minutes, and not one minute more. We have some rooms for small sessions, and any group can ask for one. If you need any help with the material, write to the office. See you soon.

extra_audio.text: Joice opens the report with the numbers of the year. She reads how many schools are in the program. She sees that there is not enough data about small schools. She writes one question about the small schools. She sends the question to the team before the meeting.

reading.rtitle: Meteoro Program -- The Year in Numbers
paras: This is a short report about our year. Read it before the meeting, and bring any question you have.
How many schools are in the program? Four hundred schools, in six states. How many teachers use the platform every week? About two thousand.
How much time does a teacher need to learn the platform? Not much: about thirty minutes. We have some short videos for the first day, and any teacher can watch them at home.
Do we have any data about the small schools? Yes, we have some, but not enough. This is our first question for the next meeting.
